This is an open continuous announcement that will remain open until September 30th, 2026 or until all vacancies are filled. Qualified applicants will be considered and referred on a regular basis as vacancies exist. The VA Midwest Health Care Network advocates for a Whole Health System of care in each of the Medical Centers.

This is an approach to healthcare that empowers and equips people to take charge of their health and well-being and live their lives to the fullest. As an employee operating in a Whole Health System of care, you will operate in a model with three core elements, seeking to create a personalized health plan for each Veteran.

This is done in the context of healing relationships and healing environments and a connection back to the Veteran's community. This aligns with the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Mission Statement to Honor America's Veterans by providing exceptional health care that improves their health and well-being.

VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory The Registered Nurse assigned to the Medical/Surgical Unit on 3 Main, is a professional nurse with a broad-based clinical knowledge that enables him/her to effectively provide care to a veteran population with widely diverse medical and surgical diagnoses.

Is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing and/or supervising direct patient care. If you wish to make a difference to those who served for us, come join our team!

The primary duties for the Medical/Surgical Registered Nurse (RN) position include but are not limited to: Manage acute and chronic illness states using whole health concepts and transformative nursing modalities. Using ICARE values, providing population specific and culturally and ethnically sensitive care.

Maintaining a caring and safe environment, coordinating the care across settings and among caregivers. Safely administers medications and assesses response to medications. Adapts treatments, procedures, and equipment based on population specific patient needs. Implement health promotion and prevention interventions.

Assist veterans in the attainment of optimal levels of functioning through rehabilitation. With hospice care, provide supportive measures for the dying patient and significant others. Communicate and interact appropriately and courteously with internal and external customers.

Maintain confidentiality of patient/employee information electronically, verbally, and written. Work and function within a safe manner including infection control and operation of equipment. Integrate and apply pertinent aspects of the Medical Center performance improvement programs into his/her professional practice.

Utilize nursing research and literature in daily practice. Work Schedule: Rotating day/night shifts, to include rotating weekends and holidays. The Clinical Informatics & Medical Technology (CLIMET) Division, under the Associate Chief of Staff. The Informatics Integrator, Registered Nurse (RN) serves as a resource for local Informatics department and Informatics Committee (ISC).

The Health Informatics Integrator works directly with facility leadership and staff to support the informatics ticketing process and overall Electronic Health Record (EHR) deployment efforts to meet the organization's modernization objectives.

Some of the Informaticists duties include but are not limited to: Collaborates with interdisciplinary team members, including other program and service leaders at the facility/practice setting and network. Works closely to establish and maintain effective relationships with all levels of Veteran Affairs (VA) staff nationwide.

Assist in directing the provision of education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization consultation. Integrate software applications for clinical services by evaluating the specific needs of the service in conjunction with the software capabilities and/or any needed modifications.

Improves efficiency and effectiveness of processes by utilizing knowledge of human factors, the usability of redesigned health information systems, and knowledge of human psychological barriers to usability. Ensuring the Federal HER ticket platform seamlessly addresses healthcare and operational needs.

The Critical Care RN assumes the following major duties and responsibilities: Charge Nurse and Preceptor competent. Competently manage patients with complex diagnosis requiring ICU treatment modalities such as continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), Intra-aortic balloon pump monitoring and care for the post open heart surgery patients.

Demonstrate ability to appropriately manage use of the FemStop, and any other external vascular closure device. Demonstrate ability to transduce pressure lines (Arterial and CVP). Demonstrates ability to appropriately manage patient on Patient Controlled Analgesia. Demonstrates ability to appropriately manage patient on ETCO2.

Demonstrates ability to respond as a Code Blue Recorder, Medication Nurse, Code Facilitator, Assistant Code Leader and Rapid Response Nurse. Demonstrates ability to operate the Zoll R series biphasic defibrillator (Advance Life Support) on a patient.

Demonstrate ability to titrate vasoactive drips appropriate for all critical care patients to achieve hemodynamic stability. Demonstrate ability to appropriately manage mechanically ventilated patients. Demonstrate safe and therapeutic care of the patient with epicardial and transvenous pacing.

Safely participates in the resuscitation of a patient during a code blue and rapid response situation. Manages the critically ill patients during and after procedures where moderate sedation is needed. Competent in reading and interpreting ECG strips; and identifying abnormal and lethal rhythms.

Strong interpersonal skills for effective information exchange and problem solving with all levels of management and staff, consultants, and outside agencies. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to quickly analyze problems, determine appropriate level of intervention, and develop and apply effective solutions.

Demonstrate organizational and project management skills, with the ability to lead a team, prioritize tasks, and see projects through from inception to completion. Participates as a member or assumes a leadership role on formal service level committees, councils, or performance improvement teams.

Assesses the patient's learning needs, learning preference, and readiness to learn. Modifies teaching approach based on knowledge of human behavior, motivations, and reactions to situations.

Assists the UPC, and the NM in the development, maintenance, and implementation of the Units Score Card, addressing process related to the feedback from All Employee Survey. Proactively makes leadership choices to prioritize Veteran-Centered needs.

Operate within allocated resources and takes the initiative to find solutions to operational challenges. Maintains knowledge and understanding of The Joint Commission requirements and ensures compliance with VA and OSHA standards.

The Critical Care Unit Registered Nurse II reports to the Critical Care Unit Nurse Manager & Assistant Nurse Manager, who is the rating official: and to the Associate Nurse Executive, Inpatient Care Services, who is the approving official. This position requires flexibility in schedule and assignment, as this is a 24/7 facility.

Experience with vasoactive drips (e.g., norepinephrine, dopamine, vasopressin). Knowledge of CRRT (Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy) and other advanced therapies.

CCRN certificate preferred. NIH Stroke Scale Certification. Advanced EKG interpretation skills. Technology & Systems Familiarity with electronic health record systems (Epic, Cerner, CPRS). Competence in telemetry and invasive monitoring systems. Leadership & Professional Development Preceptor or mentor experience for onboarding new ICU nurses.

The Nursing Officer of the Day (NOD) Registered Nurse (RN) directs position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to the management of complex patient care.

The NOD demonstrates the ability to plan and organize the delivery of care to assure continuity of care and peer accountability for practice, including access to care and discharge planning.

The NOD is skilled in the delivery of patient care and serves as the facility nursing expert at all hours to support, provide and facilitate emergency medical support throughout the facility.

The incumbent serves as the facility expert for all patient care areas in identifying escalating medical crises, environmental factors, and in allocating staffing resources appropriately throughout the facility to meet the care needs of Veterans.

The NOD uses clinical knowledge and judgment to promote staff involvement in planning, decision-making, and evaluating outcomes. They function proficiently in clinical practice and/or areas related to the assigned roles and responsibilities.

Evaluates current practice and formulates outcomes for groups of patients and/or organizational processes within an area of expertise. Guides, develops, and supports staff from a leadership perspective using professional standards of care, scientific evidence, and practice to evaluate programs and/or service activities.

The NOD is a skilled nurse who demonstrates advanced leadership at the systems level that is sustainable, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex situations. Other duties as assigned.

Assistant Nurse Manager - Community Living Center The Assistant Nurse Manager (CLC) is a self-directed nurse leader accountable to the Nursing Manager, ensuring resident-centered nursing care, staff supervision, and compliance with clinical and administrative standards.

Key Duties and Responsibilities Leadership & Oversight: Works under the Nursing Manager to ensure the 24/7 operation of the unit, providing timely, high-quality nursing care that meets accepted clinical standards.

Nursing Standards: Develops and implements nursing standards for specific resident populations in long-term care, ensuring compliance with ethical and privacy requirements. Staff Management: Plans and prioritizes work, assigns tasks based on staff capabilities, evaluates performance, provides counseling, and resolves complaints.

Recruitment & Training: Assists with interviews, selection, and hiring new staff; identifies training needs and arranges development opportunities. Regulatory Compliance: Maintains accreditation readiness, supports performance measures and ensures adherence to federal/state regulations.

Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Leads interdisciplinary groups to build relationships with professional and health-related organizations. Quality & Safety: Implements quality improvement initiatives, medication safety protocols, and patient care standards.

Werde Teil von etwas Grösserem. Arbeite mit über 2000 Spezialistinnen und Spezialisten aus mehr als 100 Berufen zusammen und ermögliche querschnittgelähmten Menschen ein selbstbestimmtes Leben. Auf dem modernen Campus in Nottwil erwartet dich eine inspirierende Atmosphäre und interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit auf Augenhöhe.
Das sind deine Aufgaben
Pflege und Betreuung von wirbelsäulenverletzen Patienten in kritischen und vielschichtig anspruchsvollen Akutphasen, von Patienten mit schwersten Atemlähmungen (Thema Weaning) sowie Patienten mit lebensbedrohlichen Erkrankungen
Versorgung und Betreuung von postoperativen Patienten
Begleitung von Querschnittgelähmten und ihren Angehörigen
Arbeiten mit intensivmedizinischen Methoden wie Hämofiltration, erweitertes hämo\-dynamisches Monitoring, differenzierten Beatmungsmethoden invasiv und nicht\-invasiv
Interdisziplinäre und interprofessionelle Zusammenarbeit mit Ärzten und allen Therapiediensten
Mitglied des internen Reanimations\-Teams
Das zeichnet dich aus
Die Kombination der Akut\- und Rehabilitationspflege siehst du als willkommene Herausforderung und du schätzt es, Neues zu lernen. Nebst der intensiv\-medizinischen und pflegerischen Qualifikation verfügst du idealerweise über Kenntnisse einer Fremdsprache (f, i, e). Du bist belastbar, aufgeschlossen, teamorientiert, kannst vernetzt denken und bringst ein hohes Mass an Einfühlungsvermögen mit. Du bist motiviert, dich am Ausbau des Weanings\-Centers aktiv zu beteiligen.
Das erwartet dich
Dich erwarten nicht nur attraktive Anstellungsbedingungen, sondern auch zahlreiche weitere Vorteile. Freu dich auf eine sinnstiftende Arbeit in einem modernen Arbeitsumfeld, flexible Arbeitszeiten und vielfältige Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten. Komm zu uns und erlebe unseren einzigartigen Spirit. Weitere Infos auf .
Über uns
Das Paraplegiker\-Zentrum in Nottwil ist eine private, national und international anerkannte Spezialklinik für Querschnitt\-, Rücken\- und Beatmungsmedizin. Als Akut\- und Rehabilitationsklinik bietet das Zentrum seinen Patientinnen und Patienten eine umfassende Betreuung und unterstützt sie ein Leben . Die Klinik gehört zur Paraplegiker\-Gruppe, die ein weltweit einzigartiges Leistungsnetz für die ganzheitliche Rehabilitation von Menschen mit Querschnittlähmung bereitstellt.

Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams suchen wir in Brugg/Windisch für das Ambulatorium für Substitutionsbehandlungen (HAG) des Zentrums für Abhängigkeitserkrankungen wir per sofort oder nach Vereinbarung Sie als
Dipl. Pflegefachfrau / Dipl. Pflegefachmann HF
60\-100%
"Das Zentrum für Abhängigkeitserkrankungen ist Teil der Klinik für Erwachsenenpsychiatrie und Psychotherapie der PDAG (Klinikdirektor Prof. Dr. med. ) und wird dual von PD Dr. med. \- Pichler, Chefärztin, und Geissberger, Leitung Pflege, geleitet.

Es behandelt Menschen mit Abhängigkeitserkrankungen einschliesslich psychischer Folge\- und Begleiterkrankungen, insbesondere Doppeldiagnosen, und deckt das Spektrum von der Schadensminderung bis zur abstinenzorientierten Behandlung ab.

Am Hauptstandort in Windisch stehen dafür drei Fachstationen mit unterschiedlichen Behandlungsschwerpunkten und tagesstationären Plätzen zur Verfügung. Ebenfalls in Windisch führt das Zentrum die substitutionsgestützte Behandlung sowie die heroingestützte Behandlung für Menschen mit Opioidabhängigkeit.

An den Standorten Aarau, Baden und Windisch bietet es ambulante suchtmedizinische Abklärungen, Behandlungen und Spezialsprechstunden an, auch bei Verhaltensabhängigkeiten. Eine Mitarbeit in laufenden klinischen Forschungsprojekten ist möglich und wird unterstützt.

Das Zentrum ist eine SIWF\-anerkannte Weiterbildungsstätte für den Schwerpunkt Psychiatrie und Psychotherapie der Abhängigkeitserkrankungen, Kategorie A, stationär und ambulant (2 Jahre für den Schwerpunkt, 1 Zusatzjahr anrechenbar an den Facharzttitel)."
Profil
Pflegefachperson HF, idealerweise mit Erfahrung in der Arbeit mit Menschen mit Abhängigkeitserkrankungen oder mit der Bereitschaft, sich dieses Fachwissen anzueignen
Sie sind eine engagierte Fachperson mit hoher Fach\-, Sozial\- und Selbstkompetenz und bringen Interesse an der aktiven Weiterentwicklung unseres Behandlungskonzepts mit
Sie arbeiten selbständig und reflektieren Ihre Tätigkeit sowie Ihr eigenes Handeln regelmässig
Sie verfügen über ein ressourcen\- und lösungsorientiertes Pflegeverständnis sowie über präzise mündliche und schriftliche Kommunikationsfähigkeiten
Sie sind eine motivierte, flexible und teamorientierte Persönlichkeit mit Humor
Aufgaben
Begleitung, Betreuung und Förderung von Menschen mit Abhängigkeitserkrankungen
Abgabe von Substitutionsmedikation
Begleitung unserer Patientinnen und Patienten im Pflegeprozess innerhalb des Bezugspersonensystems
Umsetzung unseres qualitativ hochwertigen Behandlungskonzepts
Mitarbeit in einem interdisziplinären Behandlungsteam mit Verantwortung für die Umsetzung des Behandlungsauftrags und des Leitbilds der Klinik

Unsere Mitarbeitenden sind das Herz unseres Unternehmens. Genau deshalb bieten wir Ihnen auch sehr viel: Weiterbildungen werden bei uns stark gefördert. Ebenfalls investieren wir viel in den Teamzusammenhalt und bieten allen unseren Teams den Zugang zur Software «Moodtalk» an, mit der die Teamkommunikation gestärkt wird.

Daneben bieten wir attraktive Vergünstigungen bei bekannten Marken wie Ikea, Zalando, Coop, Lidl und vielen mehr. Mitarbeitende, die mit den öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln zu uns pendeln, erhalten am Ende des Jahres einen stattlichen Öko\-Bonus ausbezahlt. Zusätzlich bieten wir eine attraktive Pensionskassenlösung an.

Für das Zentrum Forensische Psychiatrie stationär (ZFPS) suchen wir per sofort oder nach Vereinbarung Sie als
Dipl. Pflegefachfrau / Pflegefachmann HF/FH Klinik für Forensische Psychiatrie
70\-100%
Die Klinik für Forensische Psychiatrie (KFP) besteht aus der Gutachtenstelle, dem Zentrum für Forensische Psychiatrie stationär (ZFPS) und dem Zentrum für Forensische Psychiatrie ambulant (ZFPA). Von der Gutachtenstelle werden jährlich eine Vielzahl Gutachten für behördliche Auftraggeber erstellt.

Zum ZFPS gehören sechs Stationen mit insgesamt 74 Betten, auf denen psychisch kranke Straftäterinnen und Straftäter im Rahmen gerichtlich angeordneter therapeutischer Massnahmen (Art. 59 StGB) behandelt sowie Kriseninterventionen bei Patientinnen und Patienten aus Vollzugs\- und Untersuchungsgefängnissen durchgeführt werden.

Das ZFPA führt ein forensisches Ambulatorium und bietet einen gefängnispsychiatrischen Konsiliar\- und Liaisondienst an.

The Ambulatory Surgery Registered Nurse (RN) provides pre-operative/procedural care, including (but not limited to) the nursing assessment of patients, consent, and H&P validations, the starting of intravenous fluids including venipuncture, assisting with peripheral nerve blocks, assuring all lab work and other pre-operative/procedural testing is completed and communicated to team members, confirms surgical sites are prepared and marked, the administration of medications as ordered, provides clear and concise preoperative teaching and reviews discharge instructions to patients and families with written and verbal communication.

The Ambulatory RN is responsible for ensuring comprehensive documentation of all phases of care and is timely, complete, and accurate in the electronic health record.

Major components of this function include surveillance, prevention and control activities; reporting communicable illnesses; infection control policy development; administrative functions; infection control education and training; consultative services, and analysis of infection control data.

The Infection Preventionist (IP) has the authority to function in all services of the organization to coordinate, establish and monitor acceptable infection control practices and standards.

S/he serves as a principal member of the Infection Control Committee and recommends new or revised practices, based on currently accepted evidence-based infection prevention and control strategies.

The IP evaluates clinical parameters to determine the presence of infection, assess the severity of disease, identify specific risk factors, and determine source(s) for infection that can be improved.

The IP analyzes surveillance data monthly, quarterly, and annually to identify unusual occurrences, clusters of infection, infection due to unusual pathogens, and occurrence of healthcare-acquired infections that exceed the targets established for the organization, determining the need for intervention.

The IP uses standard definitions for the identification and classification of events, indicators, or outcomes and appropriate statistical techniques to describe the data, calculate rates and critically evaluate the significance of findings.

The IP analyzes data using comparative data when available and reports epidemiologically significant findings appropriately. The IP evaluates infectiousness of patients and employees with communicable diseases, makes recommendations for isolation or work restrictions, and investigates exposures to these diseases.

The IP recognizes deviations from infection control standards and makes recommendations as necessary to maintain the same level of infection control prevention and control standards throughout all areas of the organization.

The IP evaluates the effectiveness of infection prevention and control measures in assigned areas of responsibility and identifies potential infection hazards and deviations from expected hospital target for infection and/or colonization of patients.

The IP facilitates implementation of infection control policies and procedures and makes recommendations for integration of infection control principles throughout the medical center. The IP monitors implementation of infection control policies and procedures.

The IP identifies opportunities to integrate surveillance findings into the organization's plan for improvement and initiates and facilitates procedural changes to improve infection control practices through active participation and/or collaboration with appropriate committees or workgroups.

The IP takes remedial action and implements immediate infection control measures when a known breach is identified or there is reason to believe that there is danger of exposure to or spread of infection in patients or personnel. The IP communicates and follows up with all services involved to ensure corrective action is implemented.

The IP formulates individual goals for specific areas of individual responsibility to accomplish the broader goals of the Infection Control Program. The IP participates in Quality Improvement activities and contributes epidemiological skills and expert knowledge of infection prevention and control methods.

The IP uses knowledge of current scientific literature and existing regulations and guidelines to incorporate appropriate recommendations into written infection control policies and procedures and to ensure consistency with current standards of care.

The IP establishes and maintains effective oral and written communications with all services and community agencies as needed concerning prevention and control of infections in patients. The IP ensures that findings, recommendations, and policies of the infection control program are disseminated to appropriate individuals.
